checks.note: Smyth §2070: 'A circumstantial participle agreeing with a genitive noun or pronoun which is not in the main construction of the sentence, stands in the genitive absolute.' §2058 says the same. The bearing is fair: by this rule τοῦ δὲ [λόγου] would take a singular participle, as τοῦ μὲν … λόγου … παραβαλλομένου does.
The first sentence of §2148 is quoted correctly and is on that page.
checks.correction: §2148 is about anacoluthon. A participle is construed with the subject of the finite verb the writer had in mind. All its examples concern case: a nominative where an oblique case is required, partitive apposition, a nominative instead of a genitive absolute. §2148 does not use the phrase 'construction according to sense' (that is §926a and §1013) and says nothing about number or gender agreement with a dependent genitive. So it does not support b as stated. The relevant places are Smyth §§1013–1014 and Kühner–Gerth II.1 §359.5.

checks.note: §925 gives three concords, including: an adjective (and so a participle) agrees with its substantive in gender, number and case. §926 explains 'apparent violation of the concords' by (a) construction according to sense and (b) attraction.

§2072a: the genitive participle may stand without its noun when it is easily supplied from the context. §2073 (same subject as the main clause; dative replaced by a genitive absolute; subject = object of the leading verb) and §2074 (comparison with the Latin ablative absolute) concern the subject's relation to the main clause, not number. The characterization is accurate.

checks.url_used: https://fgh.perseids.org/read/greekLit/tlg1724/tlg001/1st1K-grc1/61-80 (also checked in the First1KGreek TEI tlg1724.tlg001.1st1K-grc1.xml)
checks.note: Hiller p. 66.10 prints ἀτονώτεροι καὶ ἀσθενέστεροι γινόμενοι τὴν αὐτῶν οἰκείαν δύναμιν ἔχουσι. The apparatus has: '10 ἀτονώτερος καὶ ἀσθενέστερος γινόμενος τὴν αυτοῦ δύναμιν οἰκείαν (cf. p. 65, 20. 66, 4) ἔχει κτλ. A'. Likewise at 66.5: 'κέκτηνται Bull.] κέκτηται A'. The bearing is stated fairly.

§1020: an adjective agrees with its substantive in gender, number and case, and so do participles. §1021: an attributive adjective or participle, generally with the article, often does without its substantive when that can be supplied from the context.
§2058: 'A participle agreeing in the genitive with its own subject, which is not identical with the subject of the leading verb, is said to stand in the genitive absolute.'

This is G. Gerbi's entry 'συγκρίνω, σύγκρισις (Phryn. Ecl. 243)'. At B.1 (Ioann. Sard. in Aphth. Prog. 180.19–181.10), John reports that Phrynichus prefers ἀντεξετάζειν and παραβάλλειν to σύγκρισις/συγκρίνειν. He then glosses: λόγος ἀντεξεταστικός = παραβλητικός· ἀντεξετάζειν γὰρ τὸ παραβάλλειν. So the link to παραβάλλειν comes through Phrynichus' prescription and John's gloss, not through a direct equation by John. The entry does document the later sense 'compare', from Aristotle onward and in Byzantine use. The bearing is fair.
Xen. Anab. 1.2.22 (Κῦρος ἀνέβη … οὐδενὸς κωλύοντος) is cited in both §2058 and §2070e. Isocr. 9.56 (Κόνωνος στρατηγοῦντος) is in §2070a.
§580: 'The Participle is a verbal adjective'. §580a: 'As a verb the participle has voice and tense … As an adjective it is declined, and agrees with a noun or pronoun.'

§1044: 'A circumstantial participle referring to a collective noun may be plural', with the example τὸ στράτευμα ἐπορίζετο σῖτον κόπτοντες τοὺς βοῦς (X. A. 2.1.6). §1044 also gives οὐδεὶς … πενθοῦντες (X. H. 2.2.3).

§359.4 begins at the foot of p. 57 and runs on to p. 58; the running head of p. 58 reads '§ 360'. It covers τό/τά + genitive plural, or + preposition with its case: the verb is regularly plural, and a predicate adjective is plural and takes the gender of the genitive. Examples: Pl. Civ. 563c, Leg. 657d, Phil. 45e. §359.5 (p. 58) says the participle in 'entfernterer attributiver Beziehung' agrees 'in der Regel' with the subject in case and with the genitive in gender and number. Examples: λ 90, π 476 (cf. η 67, ν 20, υ 34), B 459, P 756, λ 15, S. Ant. 1002. Counter-example: Th. 1.110 … πολεμήσαντα, 'nicht πολεμήσαντες κ. τ. σύνεσιν'. One omission: K-G also gives a second 'Aber' case, B 88 (ἔθνεα … μελισσάων … ἐρχομενάων), where the participle follows the genitive in case as well. Th. 1.110 is the only counter-example that bears on gender and number.

§1013 'Construction according to the Sense (926 a)' sits under 'Peculiarities in the use of gender'. §1014 opens 'So in periphrases': ἲς Τηλεμάχοιο … ἰδών (π 476) and τὸ δὲ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἡμῶν … χαίροντες (P. L. 657d). 'Periphrases' is the opening words of §1014, not a heading.

H 64v.15–18 reads προσηγορίαι δὲ φθόγγων διάφοροι· τῆι … λαμβάνον|τες. Par. 21v.2–6 has … διάφοροι· τῇ … λαμ|βάνοντες. V 76r.16–19 has … τῇ … λαμβάνοντες. Bas. 25.2–4 prints τῷ … λαμβάνοντος, so Bas. also differs at τῷ/τῇ. On the bearing: προσηγορίαι and λαμβάνοντες are both plural, so number is not diagnostic here. Only the masculine gender points to φθόγγων.

H 67v.19–68r.1, Par. 25r.3–7 and V 80r.8–13 all read τὸ διὰ πέντε διάστημα … λόγον ἡμιόλιον ἔχον (V ἔχων) … ἣν ἔχει πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ αὐτοῦ (V τοὺς αὐτοῦ, without πρό) συγκρινόμενος φαίνεται ἡμιόλιος. 'All witnesses' holds for the three manuscripts only: Bas. 30.5 prints πρὸς τὸν πρὸ αὐτοῦ. The predicate ἡμιόλιος is masculine too, which fits a construction by sense with λόγος.

Vincent 340.11–13: τὰ δὲ ἄμεσα … πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ αὐτῶν ἐγγὺς φθόγγους τὴν ποιὰν τῶν λόγων ἕξιν πεποίηνται. 340.16–18: τῶν ἐν αὐτοῖς κεκραμένων διαστημάτων … λογοθετηθέντων. 340.25–26: τοῦ μὲν τῶν ἐμμέσων διαστημάτων λόγου … παραβαλλομένου. Note that κεκραμένων is Vincent's emendation (340 n. 4: Ms. κεκρυμμένων). There is no note at λογοθετηθέντων or at the διαστημάτων of 340.17.

The readings quoted are correct: 338 n. 2, n. 4, n. 5, 340 n. 3, 342 n. 1, 342 n. 6. There is indeed no -ου/-ων confusion. P's μονάδος with τεμνομένων, which Vincent changed to μονάδων (342 n. 1), is confirmed.
checks.correction: The evidence has 18 notes on pp. 338, 340 and 342, of which 14 begin 'Ms.', not 17: five on p. 338, four on p. 340, five on p. 342. 338 n. 3 (Ms. ἡ σύμφρασις for τὴν σύμφρασιν) is also a case-ending error, so there are seven inflectional notes, not 'about six'. 342 n. 5 also contains 'ἀπὸ τῆ τάσεως'. μονάδων μὴ τεμνομένων (342.3–4) begins in the line right after the place (342.1–2), not two lines after.

checks.note: Kalbfleisch p. 33, lines 5–7: τῆς μὲν ἰδιότητος τοῦ ζῴου ἐν αἰσθήσει καὶ ὁρμῇ συνισταμένης, τῆς δὲ τῶν φυτῶν ἐν θρεπτικῇ τε καὶ αὐξητικῇ χωρὶς αἰσθήσεώς τε καὶ ὁρμῆς θεωρουμένης. This is exactly as described.
Book 4, chapter 4, section 17, just after <pb n="2.64"/> (Volkmann II p. 64): οἷον διττῆς πόλεως οὔσης, τῆς μὲν ἄνω, τῆς δὲ τῶν κάτω, κατὰ τὰ ἄνω κοσμουμένης.

Lemma 14 (Aph. 1.14), Kühn 17B p. 410: οὐ παραπλησίαν γε τὴν θερμὴν οὐσίαν ἐν ἀμφοτέροις αὐτοῖς ὑπάρχειν ἐροῦμεν, τῆς μὲν τῶν παίδων ὑγρᾶς οὔσης, τῆς δὲ τῶν ἀκμαζόντων ξηρᾶς. The δέ-member has no participle of its own (οὔσης is understood). Its singular is the predicate adjective ξηρᾶς.
All three passages exist.
checks.correction: Robbins' text (Perseus grc2, Tetr. 1.3) reads ἀλλ’ ὡς μὲν τῆς τῶν οὐρανίων κινήσεως … ἀποτελουμένης, τῆς δὲ τῶν ἐπιγείων ἀλλοιώσεως … λαμβανούσης. The wording 'τῆς μὲν τῶν' is that of Boll–Boer (First1KGreek). Sextus is M. 1.67 (Mau p. 18): τῆς δέ τῶν πάντων γνώσεως ἀδυνάτου τάχα καθεστώσης κεχώρισται. Here τῆς … γνώσεως is a genitive of separation governed by κεχώρισται, not a genitive absolute. Philoponus is In de An. p. 151 Hayduck. In all three the head noun is expressed, so they show only regular agreement with an expressed singular head. They are not parallels for an omitted head.

checks.note: I reproduced the search: 2,045 *grc*.xml files, about 656 MB. The pattern was τοῦ/τῆς δὲ τῶν + a genitive participle ending within 12 words. It gave 55 hits, 44 without Zonaras (tlg3135; the finding reports 46). The only cases with the head omitted and a predicate following are Ad Gaurum, Plotinus IV.4.17 and Galen, all singular. A further case the finding does not list is Josephus (tlg0526): τοῦ δὲ τῶν εἰς χλεύην ἀνακειμένων εἰπόντος, where the article is a pronoun and the participle is singular. In Eusebius (tlg2018) the plural περιδρασσομένων agrees with its own plural subject, and τῆς … πτώσεως is its object, so it is not an attraction. No plural attracted to the genitive was found.

The author is T. Janz. On ων: 'Identical in shape to a circumflex, but usually larger.' This is confirmed. Janz classes it among signs for word endings added like diacritics; he does not call it a 'suspension'.
checks.correction: For ου Janz gives two types. The first is a ligature of majuscule O and Υ, 'which is sometimes used in line'. Only 'the second type is always above the headline'. So ου is not always superscript.

checks.note: §2145: in P-B times the function of the absolute cases 'was lost sight of, and a confusion ensued'. The examples include genitive absolutes whose subject is the same as the main clause's (Mark 5:18 etc.) and nominative absolutes (Acts 19:34, Jude 16). This is confirmed. §1176: the number of the verb is often set by 'the nearest or most prominent' of several subjects. This is confirmed.
checks.correction: §1181b is narrower than 'agreement breaks down in vernacular texts'. It says that when the imparisyllabic declension retreated from popular speech, confusion followed. The examples (Acta Thomae, Theophylact) are masculine or common participle and adjective forms used with feminine nouns, e.g. αἱ χεῖρες … κηρύσσοντες, Μυγδονία ἀναστάς. That is gender, not number.

checks.note: The content is confirmed. §31.4 (pp. 81–82) says construction ad sensum affects both number and gender. The main case is collectives that sum up a plurality of persons. Examples include A 6,7 πολύς τε ὄχλος τῶν ἱερέων ὑπήκουον and A 25,24 ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐνέτυχόν μοι …, βοῶντες.
checks.correction: The archive.org item is the 3rd edition of 1911, an unchanged reprint of the 2nd, improved and enlarged, edition (1902). The page footers read '2. Aufl.' Cite it as 2nd ed. 1902, or as 3rd ed. 1911 (reprint of the 2nd), not as '2nd ed. 1911'.

summary:
I checked all 25 findings: 18 confirmed, 7 corrected, none wrong, none unreachable. I opened the Smyth sections on Alpheios and Goodell on DCC. I read Kühner–Gerth, Jannaris and Blass in the archive.org OCR, and the Atticism and Vatican Spotlight pages. I opened the Greek parallels in First1KGreek/Perseus TEI and checked the P/H/Par./V/Bas. readings in the evidence files. I also reproduced the corpus search (new-11) on fresh full downloads of both corpora.

Main corrections:
- Q11-02: Smyth §2148 is about anacoluthon in case. It does not cover agreement by sense with a dependent genitive; that is §§1013–1014 and K-G §359.5.
- new-06: Vincent has 14 'Ms.' notes, not 17. The inflectional ones are seven, adding 338 n. 3.
- new-10: in all three passages the head noun is expressed, so they are not omitted-head parallels. The Sextus passage is a genitive of separation, not a genitive absolute. 'τῆς μὲν τῶν' is the wording of Boll–Boer, not of Robbins.
- new-12: Janz's first ου form, the O-Υ ligature, can stand in line.
- new-13: Jannaris §1181b concerns gender confusion in imparisyllabic forms.
- new-14: the archive.org Blass is the 3rd ed. 1911, a reprint of the 2nd (1902).

Smaller notes:
- new-01 omits K-G's second 'Aber' case, Il. 2.88.
- new-03: number is not diagnostic there.
- new-04: Bas. prints τόν where the manuscripts have τούς.
